name: Aaron Petrov

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. What does your workday involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 58 and have managed an eight-person import-document team at a large shipping company for several years. We check container seal numbers, customs forms and arrival notices so a refrigerated load does not sit on the quay because one digit is wrong. I have a bachelor’s degree and am about average among the managers here. I use our approved AI comparison tool every day, but if the seal photograph and the form disagree I call the quay clerk before releasing the file.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: And what is the household situation?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner works variable hours at a small print shop, and our grown children live separately. We rent and have about three weeks of expenses saved. My pay is low for this manager job, and there are few comparable shipping offices nearby. I like trying new tools, but the rent needs an actual pay cheque; a port job in another region would take a household decision, not just a click on an advert.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team AI Plateau helps compare two lists of seal numbers, but the quay photograph still decides which container we have. I would keep a person on the phone for a mismatch instead of sending a tidy wrong form.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think my job survives a modest tool change. Our rent is less comfortable: my partner’s print-shop hours vary, and three weeks saved is barely a buffer. A quiet AI future does not lengthen a short pay month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep our daily seal-photo call with the quay clerk when a number does not match. I would continue using the approved AI comparison but check the original photograph before signing a release. If this mild change arrives next year, I would keep that routine and make the rent payment before any optional spending.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the household cash, not the comparison tool. A wrong release can strand a refrigerated container, and a short print-shop rota can strand our rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What mismatch stays with you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A chilled-fruit container had a seal ending in 19, while the copied manifest ended in 91. The software marked the two lines as close enough to review later. We held the file, called the quay clerk and kept the truck from turning up at the wrong gate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Do you use AI to decide the release?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I use the comparison every day to find where to look, then inspect the photograph and call. The company pays us to release the right container, not the fastest plausible number.

say: An **AI comparison** helps find mismatches, but a seal photograph decides the release.
I would keep **quay calls** for disputed numbers.
think: My **experienced post** looks stable under a modest tool change.
Variable **print-shop hours** and three weeks saved threaten rent even without AI.
do: **Keep** daily seal-photo calls for mismatched container numbers.
**Use** the approved comparison only before checking the original photograph.
**Pay** rent before optional spending in a short-pay month.
feel: I feel **anxious** about cash while the job itself looks steady.
S0.quote: A chilled-fruit container had a seal ending in 19, while the copied manifest ended in 91.
fieldNote: His **daily AI use** is an established comparison routine with a physical seal check.
The **three-week reserve** and variable partner hours make baseline rent risk real.

steps.text: Keep calling quay clerk when container seal numbers disagree
Use approved comparison then check original seal photograph before release
Pay rent before optional spending in short-pay months

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues stronger AI can compare manifests and write clearance notes, so the company could cut document posts. I would ask the union to count delays caused by wrong releases as well as faster files. Nobody at the quay is paid for a number that only looks right.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think one experienced manager might run two document teams, and my post could be one of the ones combined. I am quick with new tools, but that does not guarantee a manager wage. Three weeks saved makes me unwilling to wait for a perfect local vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next week I would give our union representative six held-container records, with the wrong digit and the actual delay. I would ask management to keep a paid human sign-off on mismatched seals and make the error count visible on our shift board. If an advertised document role opens at the inland freight hub, I would apply only if its net pay after travel covers our rent; I would not accept or move until there is a firm offer and my partner agrees that the household can relocate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a combined team and annoyed that an error can be made invisible in a speed report. I can talk to the union and look farther afield, but neither is a wage yet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would six records prove?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One wrong digit might be an isolated mistake; six show whether the same copying step is failing. I would include the time the refrigerated load waited, because the loss is not just an office correction. A ripe load cannot sit on the quay while two systems argue.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your partner move for an advert?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. They have work here, even if the hours vary, and an advert is not a contract. We would compare the actual wage, moving costs and their likely work before deciding together.

say: **Manifest automation** needs delay costs counted alongside fast clearances.
I would take **six held loads** to the union.
think: Two document teams under **one manager** could remove my post.
Three weeks saved cannot fund a long **local search**.
do: **Give** the union six held-container records next week.
**Request** paid human sign-off and visible errors for mismatched seals.
**Apply** to an advertised inland-hub role only with rent-covering net pay; move only after firm offer and partner agreement.
feel: I feel **anxious** about consolidation and hidden delay costs.
S1.quote: A ripe load cannot sit on the quay while two systems argue.
fieldNote: He uses **delay evidence** and union channels while actively scanning a wider job market.
An **inland move** needs actual pay, relocation costs, partner agreement and a firm offer.

steps.text: Give union six held-container cases with wrong digits and delays
Apply for advertised inland-hub role only with rent-covering net pay after travel
Move only after firm offer partner agreement and checked relocation costs

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew AGI by 2028 could write customs forms and choose releases before workers know who is answerable for a wrong container. I would ask for written notice and a named person who can halt a mistaken release.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect document teams to lose posts quickly, and mine could go. Another freight-paperwork desk faces 2028 AGI too. Moving containers with cranes is physical until capable robots arrive around 2031, but I do not have the licence or an offer for that work. Three weeks saved means a long argument over responsibility would be unaffordable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would ask the union for severance terms and a written stop-release rule. I would check our rent dates and my partner’s actual print-shop pay, not shifts pencilled onto next month’s rota. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I am cut, I would apply for posted regional document or dispatch jobs only with rent-covering net pay; I would move only with my partner’s agreement, a confirmed offer and a realistic plan for both our incomes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because a few weeks of cash will not last through a fast closure. I can widen the search, but I cannot make a new port job exist by wanting it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would crane work buy three years?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not for me without training, a licence, safe practice and a vacancy. Robots for physical work come around 2031 in this picture. A document manager cannot climb into a crane and claim the wage tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if your partner says no to moving?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then we stay and search the local options or travel only if the net pay works. Their print-shop work is part of our income, even when the hours are uncertain. I would not decide for both of us.

say: **2028 AGI** needs notice and a human stop-release rule.
I would seek written **severance terms** for document teams.
think: My **own post** could go in fast document cuts.
Other desks face **2028 AGI**; physical cranes face robots around 2031.
do: **Ask** union this month for severance and stop-release terms.
**Check** rent dates against actual print-shop wages.
**Apply** for posted regional jobs with rent-covering net pay after travel; move only with partner consent, firm offer, both-income plan.
feel: I feel **alarmed** because three weeks saved cannot fund a long closure.
S2.quote: A document manager cannot climb into a crane and claim the wage tomorrow.
fieldNote: He rejects **crane work** as an unlicensed, unoffered fallback despite later physical robots.
His **partner’s pay** and consent matter to relocation, and a thin reserve raises urgency.

steps.text: Ask union for written severance and human stop-release authority
Apply after cut to posted regional jobs only with rent-covering net pay
Move only with partner consent firm offer and plan for both incomes

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years lets the company agree who can stop a wrong release and give document staff paid chances to learn the new systems. I would not sell crane work as a safe escape just because robots arrive later.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I might find work at an inland freight hub if I can learn its procedures, but its planning and dispatch screens face 2031 AGI too. Physical loading robots follow around 2034. At 63 I do not know whether our actual retirement income could pay the rent, and relocating might cost more than we have saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2027 I would ask the inland hub for an interview and a written pay range for its posted dispatch role; I would travel for the interview only if the company covers the fare or I can pay without missing rent. I would take the role only after a confirmed offer, a net wage that supports our rent and move costs, and my partner’s agreement on work there. After 2031 I would keep doing paid document checks if that work exists rather than count the hub as an assured refuge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the desk but grateful for five years to investigate a real opening. I would not move our home based on a pay range alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask at the hub?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Whether I would be dispatching trucks on a screen or checking loads in the yard, and who signs a stop when a seal is wrong. The screen work faces AGI by 2031 too. I would ask the manager to show the actual shift and salary in writing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use savings for the move?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after a firm offer and after we calculate the deposit, travel and any gap in my partner’s wages. We have three weeks saved, so I cannot make a speculative move. An interview is information, not a new household.

say: A **five-year runway** should bring stop-release authority and paid systems learning.
I would reject **crane work** as an automatic refuge.
think: Inland dispatch screens face **2031 AGI**, with physical loading robots around 2034.
At **63**, retirement pay and moving costs are unknown.
do: **Request** an interview and written pay range for a posted inland-hub dispatch role.
**Travel** for interview only with funded fare or after rent is secure.
**Accept** only a firm offer with net rent-and-move pay and partner agreement.
feel: I feel **anxious** about desk loss but able to investigate an actual opening.
S3.quote: An interview is information, not a new household.
fieldNote: He separates **interview and offer** stages, with fare and rent protection before travel.
An **inland dispatch desk** faces the same 2031 thinking exposure, and relocation requires partner consent.

steps.text: Request interview and written pay for posted inland-hub dispatch role
Travel for interview only if fare funded or rent remains secure
Accept firm offer only with net rent-and-move pay and partner agreement
Move only after firm offer affordable costs and partner consent

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the company a decade is enough to write a worker’s right to halt a false release into contracts and pay for training where jobs actually exist. I would ask the union to test the promise against real vacancies.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I will be 68 in 2036. I may want to stop, but I have not checked any retirement entitlement or net amount, and three weeks saved is no bridge. Customs forms and dispatch screens face 2036 AGI; physical container moves meet robots around 2039. My partner and I cannot plan on a grown child paying our rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep the photograph check and ask for an actual retirement-income statement, then compare verified income and savings with rent and bills. I would set aside twenty extra only after my wage and my partner’s actual pay arrive, rent and utilities clear, and no print-shop shift has been cancelled. After 2036 I would keep paid work if verified retirement income plus savings cannot meet our bills; I would search posted work if my document role ends.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about whether there will be wages at 68. Ten years gives time to ask and save, but our present three-week buffer is small.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why only twenty?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A cancelled shop shift can take more than twenty from the month. I would transfer new earnings only after rent is paid, not move existing cash from one account to another. We would skip it whenever the actual pay is short.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if retirement pay is enough?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner and I would compare the verified amount plus savings with our real bills before stopping. I have not seen the statement yet. I will not promise the children we can manage on an estimate.

say: A **decade** should bring stop-release rights and paid training tied to vacancies.
I would ask the **union** to check real openings.
think: At **68**, retirement income and eligibility remain unverified.
Document desks face **2036 AGI**, with physical container robots around 2039.
do: **Save** twenty extra only after both actual wages, rent and utilities clear with no cancelled shop shift.
**Continue** paid work after 2036 if verified retirement income plus savings cannot pay bills.
feel: I feel **anxious** about future wages and today’s short reserve.
S4.quote: I would transfer new earnings only after rent is paid, not move existing cash from one account to another.
fieldNote: His **twenty transfer** adds new earnings only after actual wages and essential bills.
He makes no **retirement entitlement** or child-support assumption despite a decade of warning.

steps.text: Keep checking seal photographs before document release
Save twenty only after both actual wages rent utilities and no cancelled shop shift
Continue paid work after 2036 if verified income plus savings cannot meet bills
Search posted work if document role ends

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. A document office could close before we have enough cash for a move or a long search. Written notice, a human stop-release rule and real jobs with net wages we can live on would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask my partner about any relocation before counting it as my plan. A wrong seal digit can hold a container; a wrong wage estimate can hold a household. I would verify both before signing.

headlineQuote: A wrong seal digit can hold a container; a wrong wage estimate can hold a household.
portrait: **Aaron, 58**, is an experienced import-document manager supervising eight people at a large shipping company.
His **low pay**, variable print-shop partner, three-week reserve and few nearby roles leave rent exposed.
He uses **AI daily** to compare manifests but checks physical seal photographs before release.
He is **anxious** even under mild change, alarmed by fast desk cuts and explores relocation only with partner consent.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could close his document post before the household can fund a long search.
whatWouldHelp: Written **notice**, human stop-release authority and firm bill-paying job offers would help.
